lines.speaker: Cnemon
lines.text: Well — there's the proverb come true. The fawn hunts down the lion.
lines.description: bitterly amazed, dry proverb as self-indictment

lines.speaker: Cnemon
lines.text: You're asking what's eating me? I've left an heir I never meant to leave — outwitted, the poor fool that I am — and the people I actually wanted to inherit got nothing.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.description: plain, inviting the story without sympathy

lines.speaker: Cnemon
lines.text: Hermolaus — you know, the enormously rich one, no children — I'd been courting him with an eye on his deathbed, and he wasn't unhappy to be courted. So I had what I thought was a clever idea: I drew up a will, very publicly, leaving everything I owned to him. The point being he'd be flattered, follow suit, and do the same for me.

lines.speaker: Cnemon
lines.text: What he put in his own will, I have no idea. What I can tell you is that the roof fell in on me, [pause] and now Hermolaus has the lot. Swallowed me whole — like some big fish that gulps down the hook along with the bait.
lines.description: rueful precision, then stunned at the absurdity

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: Not just the hook, Cnemon. The fisherman too. You've out-schemed yourself.
lines.description: deadpan correction, savoring the neat punchline

lines.speaker: Cnemon
lines.text: [sighs] So it seems. Hence the wailing.
lines.description: deflated, accepting he is the joke
